summary: FBRX 2.1.2 Beta: sign in to FBRX Command on the same computer, the FBRX Browser on your home network, a Fabrix that knows its budget and builds with care, and Hermes Agent in AI coordination.
notes: Sign in to FBRX Command running on this computer or your home network (https://127.0.0.1:8787 or its address): FBRX shows the certificate's fingerprint, and once you trust it, sign-in, invitations and FBRX Cloud AI use that certificate only.

The FBRX Browser opens IP addresses, names with a port and local names (127.0.0.1:8080, 192.168.1.20, nas.local). A home server with its own certificate shows its fingerprint to trust for the session; a page that only answers on http:// offers to open it that way.
Fabrix builds alongside you and leaves what it touches better: it does no harm whoever asks, tells you what else it noticed that needs fixing, and only says it did something a tool confirmed.

The context gauge under the chat shows the context window and how much of it the conversation uses. Long conversations fold their older turns into a short digest that keeps names, ids and decisions, and Fabrix paces itself and warns you as it nears the limit.

AI usage (in Connect) shows the tokens used this month and before, by model, and what is left of FBRX Cloud AI. Settings → Agent → Thinking sets a monthly budget for cloud models: Fabrix stops cleanly when it is reached.
Ask Fabrix to create a project and add a note to it and it does: workspace.create_project makes the project, and a name that does not exist is reported instead of guessed.
Pictures: image.compose draws storybook scenes from FBRX's own art (people, animals, a dragon, trees, castles, a sky by day or night) with helmets, crowns, swords and shields where you ask for them.
AI coordination connects Hermes Agent: FBRX adds itself to ~/.hermes/config.yaml and leaves the rest of the file as it was; run /reload-mcp in Hermes to load the FBRX tools.
FBRX OS for Mac is back: a .dmg for Apple silicon (arm64) and Intel (x64) Macs, with the Windows and Linux installers.

server.summary: FBRX Server 1.2.2: support passes from a computer's page in FBRX Command, and the server's Fabrix with the same 2.1.2 rules and tools.
notes: FBRX Command: a computer's page shows its install id and makes a support pass for it (Devices → the computer → Support pass).
Fabrix on the server (the ai role) gets FBRX OS 2.1.2's rules, folded history, create_project and image.compose.
From 1.1: sudo fbrx-server update check, then sudo fbrx-server update commit.

command.summary: FBRX Command 2.1.2: support passes from a computer's page, and computers on the same machine join with a trusted certificate.
notes: Support pass: open Devices, pick the computer, and choose Support pass: its install id is filled in, so the code works at the 418teapotadmin prompt on that computer.
Each computer reports its install id, shown on its page.
FBRX OS on the same computer as FBRX Command signs in and accepts invitations at https://127.0.0.1:8787 after trusting its certificate's fingerprint.
